summary: the case of tests/run make on i686, against a utimensat that leaves a file's modification time on the KRFFS root as it was, and a kernel whose real time starts at the same second at every boot in place of the real-time clock's reading

argv: ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 && ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel

faults.name: touch-ignored
faults.summary: a lost time: utimensat on the KRFFS root succeeds and leaves the modification time as it was, so touching the header rebuilds nothing; a write still gives the file the present time

edits.find:
kn->modification_time.seconds = now ? now_sec : times[1].tv_sec;
        kn->modification_time.nanoseconds = now ? now_nsec : times[1].tv_nsec;

lines: machine.make.rebuild on i686: failure: header failed: touching the shared header did not rebuild both objects

faults.name: clock-restarts
faults.summary: a clock that restarts: every boot anchors real time at the same second, 1700000000, in place of the real-time clock's reading, so a source changed after the reboot is older than the object built before it

lines: machine.make.rebuild on i686: failure: reboot-change failed: a source changed after a reboot did not rebuild: the clock restarted
